claim: The EU Migration Pact forces the Baltic states to accept migrants from other EU countries
claimed_by: Populist politicians and social media posts in the Baltic states
conflict: The Pact lets each country choose between taking people, paying or giving other support; Latvia and Lithuania have said they will not take relocated migrants, and fewer than 1,000 people are expected to be relocated across the whole EU in 2026.
verdict_note: The rules and the published pledges contradict it.

claim: Latvia will have to take 10,000 migrants a year or pay 200 million euros
claimed_by: Latvian populist politicians before the 2024 European elections (fact-checked by Re:Baltica)
conflict: Re:Baltica found the estimate for Latvia at the time was 99 people or 2 million euros; the agreed 2026 pool for the whole EU is 21,000 relocations or equivalent support.
verdict_note: An older claim that still circulates; the figures were wrong by about a hundred times.

claim: Belarusian border officials help organise illegal migration into Latvia
conflict: Belarus has not responded to this specific case; the evidence comes from an ongoing criminal investigation.
verdict_note: Consistent with documented state organisation of migration from Belarus since 2021, but not yet tested in court.

claim: Migrants are forced to damage Latvian border equipment if they cannot pay smugglers
conflict: Based on testimony gathered in an ongoing investigation; no independent confirmation yet.
verdict_note: Credible and specific, but still under investigation.
